rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = banned register words reaching students; absent. Body view greps: banned_words 0, em_dash 0, leverage_verb 0 (all CLEAN, planted-proof); own grep '\blandscape' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = ritual/ceremony naming the activity; absent. View grep ritual_ceremony -> 0; own grep '[Pp]ractice' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = changelog in a block that should state present fact; absent. Body greps session_biography 0, dated_line 0. Closest: L115 'the beat sheet's trainer-built "two hidden false claims per group" is not used' is a negative-present sentence, but the beat sheet is a live source a later editor could re-apply, so the guard has a named pull and stays. L110 Quality line is the licensed dated-provenance form; no transition verbs (relocated, renamed, previously) in L110-131.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = wrong register (poster, consultancy, cold-tech). Voice contract = Agents 101 trio (APT101 audience is PO/PM/designer). Closest: L63 'Your main session stays blind, so it cannot quietly help the checks along' - peer-warm, concrete, a Sutherland-style reframe of why not to look; no retain-this wrapper (grep 'Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget' on body.txt -> 0), no atmospheric imagery, no we-refuse callout to contradict.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 3:'**Time:** 60 minutes. Phase 1 ~10, Phase 2 ~7, Phase 3 ~18, Phase 4 ~10, Phase 5 ~10, close ~5.' Sub-rule 'Timing location by surface' (Total ONLY). Harm present: the breakdown is a second copy of the per-phase italic markers at L23, L39, L60, L82, L94 and goes stale on the next phase edit; 'Phase 1' etc. are also ordinals. Sibling APT101 exercises carry the total only (sed -n 3p over curriculum/exercises/apt101-*.md). Creator-name and author-we greps -> 0.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut line 3 to the total: '**Time:** 60 minutes.' (the per-phase italic markers already carry the numbers; re-run calculate-time --check)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = third-person student voice / delivery mechanics in body. View grep the_student -> 0. Closest: L9 'The team lead runs the benchmark on their laptop' is a trio role, not 'the student'; L64 'the team lead reads the four methods aloud' is the group beat's own move (workshop beat), not a trainer-delivery instruction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = maintainer term of art leaking unearned. Closest: L29/L33 'claim pool' - earned at L33 ('a pool of claims the checks can score') before L41 'the same claim pool'; 'scorer' earned at L62 ('A fifth agent checks every claim ... and measures each method'); 'Known limit' glossed at L88. 'adjudicat*', 'ensemble', 'detector' appear only inside registry fences. No term found only in the maintainer block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = reassurance sentences signalling defensiveness. grep 'no penalty|fine way|it.s OK|not a downgrade|not on the hook' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: raw L29 'It is enough for the checks to have work to do.' justifies the dose rather than absolving the reader; offered as a cut in suggestions (duplicates the fence).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a slogan overpromising with no boundary. Closest: L96 'The briefing was built to be caught. Your real summary was not.' is a factual contrast, and the next sentences give the move; no slogan needing a carve-out paragraph.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = positioning posture imported into a teaching beat. grep 'vendor|not an aspirational|grounded in actual|not theoretical' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: L7 'Four ways of checking compete' - a method contest, not a defence of the training.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = operational copy lifting vocabulary above the arc. Closest: L25 lead-in says 'a separate worker' and L15 'before any judge exists' - judge is earned in the Day 2 arc before this exercise and glossed again at L84; L70 lead-in 'explain the two columns' deliberately avoids precision/recall, which arrive in the fence and the scoreboard.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a closer pronoun with two possible referents. Closest: L102 'tell your two teammates which line it was' - 'it' resolves to the flagged claim the fence ends on ('End with the one flagged claim most likely to have reached a decision unchecked'), the only line in play; L106 'Its Known limit line' - the judge file and the winning check are the same object.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 106:'It found something in a summary nobody planted anything in, and two of you know whether it caught the claim you would have bet on.' Harm present: failure mode (a), the recap asserts what the instructions do not guarantee. The maintainer note at L125 says 'Phase 5: the real summary comes back clean. That is a result, not a failure', so the sentence is false in the clean case; no accept-note covers it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Make the recap true either way: say the judge ran on a summary nobody planted anything in (see suggestion).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = talking down to the agent. grep 'bark|order|command|whip|force|drag|boss|scold|lecture' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: L43 'stop it, steer it narrower' - peer-flat steering verbs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a header a precise reader could call false. Closest: L58 '## Phase 3: Let the scorer decide' - the scorer does produce the verdict the room then reads; L11 'While the benchmark runs: ready your real summary' is literally true (phases 1-3 run on the team lead's laptop while the other two work).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = empty negation / deictic drumroll / label echo. Closest: L7 'You don't hunt for them by hand.' - the reader's actual prior is hunting by hand, so the negation is needed once; L102 '"The agent got this wrong" is the sentence.' names a concrete phrase, resolves its antecedent. No bold-label echo (L31 '**Don't open the briefing.** Your main session stays blind' does not restate its label).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 43:'All four run at once.' and 56:'Don't read the four files as they land.' sit directly under/after the four-detector fence that lists the four methods and four output files, and under the header 'Run four checks'. Harm present: a second copy of a count the fence and header already hold; adding or dropping a detector silently falsifies both lines. Kept: header numeral, L7 'Four ways of checking' and L64 'the four methods' (memory handles reused away from the list), L106 'Four checks ran'.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the numerals at L43 and L56 (see suggestions).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a false-as-stated superlative surviving as a slogan. Closest: L7 'a scorer measures which one caught what' and L62 'checks every claim' - scoped to the benchmark's own 30-claim pool, not a claim about how the world works; L63 'it cannot quietly help' is true by construction (blind main session).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a how-you'd-know clause pointing at a self-witnessing artifact. Closest: L90 'When the judge is right' - the test is L88's (under twenty lines, Known limit line naming one kind of claim let through), so it points at observable properties; L102 points at the outcome (did the judge catch the claim you bet on). Optional sharpening offered in suggestions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory rule (own text: 'Not a REVISE on its own'). Closest: raw L29 'It is enough for the checks to have work to do.' restates the fence's 'so the detectors have something to catch' (class b, restating an adjacent artifact); no superlative so rule 21 does not own it. Offered as a cut in suggestions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose stands without the trainer — no cue-card prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = trainer-cue prose failing the muted read. Muted read of L41, L43, L64, L68: each sentence has a verb and a page-named subject (L41 'Each check is a different method...', L43 'All four run at once. If one starts reading...'). Closest: L64 'Face down until the scoreboard lands.' - elliptical but 'post-it' is named in the sentence before; grep 'before it runs' hits L64, where 'it' resolves to 'A fifth agent' in L62 (a noun on the page).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = corrective gap / assumed ability tier. grep 'at your scale|for a beginner|more experienced|a senior' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: L68 'whoever missed says what they trusted instead' - names a normal miss, asks for what was trusted, not a deficiency.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = cold technical word stopping the reader. Closest: 'scorer' earned at L62 before L64/L66 use it; 'judge' glossed at L84; 'subagent' (L41, rt-code span) pairs with 'agent' for Cowork and is working vocabulary in the training's earlier exercises; precision/recall arrive in the fence and L70 'explain the two columns'. grep 'M[0-9]|Module [0-9]' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = SVP-flinch word. Closest: 'subagent' L41 (code-runtime span only; Cowork reads 'agent'). Banned-list words in jargon-ban.md checked against body.txt: embeddings/vector/RAG/retrieval/pipeline/orchestration/schema/architecture/token/context window -> 0 hits ('retrievals' in L9 is ordinary-English plural of the Day 1 retrieval step).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = memory/context blur. Closest: L9 'Your three memories were curated from the same retrievals' - memory used as the persistent artefact; the word 'context' does not appear in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = FAQ clutter in the golden path, or a deleted needed rescue. Closest: L43 'If one starts reading far beyond the evidence, stop it, steer it narrower' - plausible failure (a detector wandering) plus a non-obvious rescue, so it stays in body per the boundary clause; no below-fence routing needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = over-specified shape. Closest: the scoreboard column list in the scorer fence - a scoring format, the case the rule allows when the teaching moment depends on it (the column names are what L70 explains).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = another module's mood imported. Closest: L63-64 and L68 (blind session, post-its face down) are the benchmark's own suspense, consistent with the Agents 101 M5 source this reuses; no joyful-creation register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = error-catching handed to the student by hand; absent. Closest: L15 'Read it where you know the material best ... say which claim you would bet is unsupported before any judge exists' - the student's bet is the measured human prior, checked by the judge at L98 ('Ask Claude to run the judge'), not a substitute for it. Addressees named: L64 post-it, L68 the trio, L102 'tell your two teammates'. L88 gives object (the judge file) and tell ('describe one kind of claim this judge will let through'). No attitude adverbs (grep 'carefully|closely|thoroughly' -> 0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -i 'what research says' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = student made a mechanic outside the conversation; absent in substance. Closest: L90 'the team lead copies `judges/groundedness-judge.md` and `module-5/`' leaves the mechanism open while the next sentence says 'ask Claude to copy', implying a hand copy for the lead. One file and one folder, not the forcing function (the benchmark in chat). Rule question for the maintainer, not filed: whether the lead's copy should also route through Claude; the technical class owns whether the copy works.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = sub-clause em-dashes slowing the read. Body view grep em_dash -> 0 (CLEAN, planted-proof). Registry fences carry em-dashes (awk over expanded.md fences, grep -c '—' -> 15) but fenced prompt text is outside the writing body scope. Rule question for the maintainer: whether the shared hallucination-bakeoff prompts owe the same ban.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a doing-section headed by a noun phrase, or Claude as a header actor. Headers: 'Plant the claims', 'Run four checks', 'Let the scorer decide', 'Keep the winner', 'Run it on something real', 'Take stock' - all student verbs; closest 'Let the scorer decide' keeps the student as the verb's actor and names the agent role, not the product.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 13:'*Designer and product owner, while phases 1 to 3 run*'; 15:'Pick the summary you will check in phase 5'; 19:'when the scoreboard lands in phase 3'; 64:'from the phase 2 files'. Harm present: ordinals are coordinates; inserting or splitting a phase silently repoints four references and the reader counts to resolve them. Module abbreviations and counts of real things are exempt; these are neither.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Refer by what the section is (the end, the scoreboard, the check files) or drop the reference; see suggestions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a curriculum word colliding with a Claude Code primitive on first authored use. Closest: L9 'memories' - not authored in this exercise (curated on Day 1); 'skill'/'rule'/'plan' do not appear in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = assistant-shaped framing in agent-shaped curriculum. Body 'Claude' occurs as addressee ('Ask Claude to ...' at L15, L25, L33, L70, L74, L84, L98) and once as actor (L7); 'agent' carries the autonomous work (L62 'A fifth agent checks', L102 'The agent got this wrong'). Closest: L7 'Claude writes a briefing' - active stance, offered as a swap in suggestions; not an audit-signal ratio.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = noun-run for an agent sitting. grep -nE '\brun\b' on body.txt: L9/L41/L43/L98 are verb uses ('runs the benchmark', 'run in its own', 'All four run at once', 'run the judge'); no noun-run; L9 uses the session/task fork spans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = pinning a module to a time-of-day or gap; absent in substance. Only hit: L15 'the overnight digest' (grep -nE 'tomorrow|overnight|this morning|tonight|yesterday|last night' on body.txt -> 1). It is the fixed name of a Day 1 artefact used across sibling exercises, not a claim about when this exercise runs. Rule question for the maintainer: whether an artefact name containing a time word is exempt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = announcing that reflection is happening. grep 'sit with|let it land|take a moment|pause and reflect|Step back|Meta-moment' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: L104 '## Take stock' - the closing label across the training's exercises (10 exercise files carry the header per grep -l '^## Take stock'), over a statement recap rather than a reflection prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = meta-loop asking the student for what they already decided. Closest: the surprise prompt (L74-76) asks which scoreboard row surprised them - a fresh observation on the live scoreboard, not a restatement of a decision or of the agent's proposal; L15 asks for the bet before any judge exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '\.txt|\.docx|\.html' on body.txt -> 0; every saved artefact in the expanded fences is .md.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = true-but-useless clauses. Closest: L9 'Your three memories were curated from the same retrievals, so one benchmark speaks for all three' tells the designer and product owner why they do not run their own benchmark, which changes what they do. Raw L29's second sentence is the one near-NVA clause (offered as a cut in suggestions); the L106 recap is carried under check_writing 16.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = 'read it' narrating what the student already does after a chat print. grep -iE 'read it|look at it|study the|notice the' on body.txt -> 1 hit, L15 'Read it where you know the material best' - the student's own source summary before any chat print exists, so not dead weight after a print. Closest after a print: L88 'Open `judges/groundedness-judge.md`. Under twenty lines...' - names object and tell, a check not a read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = training or a coach imperative as the forward subject. Closest: L19 'Then join the team lead's screen when the scoreboard lands' - student as subject; L106 closes on 'Its Known limit line says what it still won't see' - an artefact as subject of a present-tense fact, no forward gesture at the training or other roles.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a neutral synonym replacing the house frame. Closest: L7 'Four ways of checking' and L25 'checks' use the training's own word for verification (checks); L102 uses the training's norm phrase 'The agent got this wrong'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = student cast as key-presser. Closest: L43 'then say *"continue"*' - say + a quoted utterance is the training's established prompt trigger per the 2026-09-03 widening, though 'continue' is the filler case the rule names. Restored on purpose by the maintainer (commit dd242fd9, 'fan-out steer restored'). Rule question, not filed; a prompt-noun swap is offered in suggestions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = walking professionals through trivial mechanics. No install, login or setting recipes in body; L90 names the copy outcome only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = the training describing its own arc. grep -nE 'later module|next module|Day [0-9]|the training' on body.txt -> 0. Closest: L9 subject is the student's memories and benchmark; L106 subject is the student's checks and file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a scaffold the student should have produced. Every artefact (roster, briefing, claim pool, detectors, judge) is produced by the student's own prompts; the only seeded paths are the Day 1 trees named in the fences.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Squint on headers alone: 'Catch it making things up / While the benchmark runs: ready your real summary / Plant the claims / Run four checks / Let the scorer decide / Keep the winner / Run it on something real / Take stock' recovers: plant fabrications, race four checks, keep the winner, try it on a real summary. H1 names the failure-hunt rather than the kept judge file, but the headers recover the build at 'Keep the winner'; a title rename is a separate pass.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-study is invisible in the training flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -iE 'self-study|Teacher Claude' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = student must edit the prompt before pasting. Closest: 'team/<my-name>/' in the two apt101-d2 fences (markers L17, L100) is the training's path template that Claude resolves, not a slot the student edits; the only slot is the deliberate open-hook 'The summary:' (fix d). Rule question: Day 1 prompts add 'Ask my first name if you don't know it' at first use and these two rely on it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 66:{{prompt:hallucination-bakeoff-5}} is preceded by L64 'Face down until the scoreboard lands.' - a hold instruction, not a command-verb lead-in. The semantic summary (L62 'A fifth agent checks every claim ...') sits two paragraphs up, declarative, with the post-it step between. Harm present: the skim-cue is separated from a 30-line fence and the student reaches it with no instruction to run it. Phase 2 fences are not filed: L41 is a one-paragraph summary of the fence directly under the header. Other lead-ins open on 'Ask Claude to' (L25, L33, L70, L74, L84, L98).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a command-verb lead-in immediately before the scorer marker (see suggestion).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = chrome the renderer owns. Every prompt is a {{prompt:key}} marker on its own line preceded by a blank line (L17, L27, L35, L47, L52, L66, L72, L76, L86, L100); label and destination chip come from the registry; both rt forks keep '*(Claude Code)*' per rule 10.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = filename drift across chained prompts. Chain is by deterministic path: briefing.md -> claim-pool.md -> detectors/*.md -> scoreboard.md -> judges/groundedness-judge.md -> judge-run.md, each fence naming the path the prior one saved (e.g. 'Open `module-5/briefing.md`').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a prompt pre-doing or deferring the next prompt's job. Closest: the detector fence's 'The scorer uses strict substring match; paraphrased findings count as misses' leaks the scorer, but the output format is load-bearing for the contest and the maintainer Watch-fors name it. Planter fence 'so the detectors have something to catch' is the instrument's dose, also pedagogically load-bearing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a reset breaking scrollback-dependent phases. grep -E '/clear|new session|fresh session' on the expanded fences -> 0; isolation uses subagents.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = literal asterisks in the pasted prompt. awk over expanded.md fence lines, grep -c '\*' -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = runtime forks drifting beyond mechanics. L45-54 paired rt-code/rt-cowork divs with the shared '*(Claude Code)*' chip; the two fences differ only in 'subagent'/'agent' (expanded.md lines 98 vs 119).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry — MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a Cowork fork thinner than the Code fork. The two detector fences are the same length; no Cowork-specific mechanics are removed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = format-only citations. Closest: the judge-run fence asks to 'quote the sentence from the source that supports it exactly, with its file path, or write "not found"' and the scorer fence 'Quote the evidence line or file that supports the label' - sentence-level integrity check present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory everywhere (2026-09-08). No plan-mode fence in this file (grep 'permission-mode: plan' -> 0).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no prompt asks Claude to interrogate its own work

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory (narrowed 2026-09-03): never gates. Closest: the judge-writing fence (L86) assembles an artefact downstream beats read and closes without a grill line; no run showed a downstream re-run caused by a save-time gap, so no finding.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = naked filenames piling at the root. Every Save/Write names a subpath: 'team/<my-name>/real-summary.md', 'module-5/evidence-roster.md', 'module-5/scoreboard.md', 'judges/groundedness-judge.md', 'team/<my-name>/judge-run.md'; one inline case 'Save the scoreboard to module-5/scoreboard.md' is unquoted but still a subpath.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a second source of truth for the working directory. grep -E '/Users|cd |~/' on the expanded fences -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = a subagent unexplained. Closest: the planter fence spawns a subagent; raw L31 'Your main session stays blind, so it cannot quietly help the checks along' explains why, after the fence. The detector fence's why is L41 ('Each check is a different method ... run in its own subagent').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = (c)-only writes bloating disk. Every Save has a named downstream reader: real-summary.md is read by the judge-run prompt ('The summary and its sources are in team/<my-name>/real-summary.md'); briefing, claim-pool and detector files by the later prompts; scoreboard by the judge-writing prompt; judge-run.md lands in the team folder the trio shares and L102 sends teammates to its flagged line.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = custom labels breaking decoratePrompts. Prompts enter only through registry markers (rule 31), so the label is generated as '**Prompt** *(dest)*'; grep '\*\*Prompt:' on body.txt -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm = orchestration bloat on a normal work request. The planter and detector fences are the benchmark protocol, which IS the lesson (the maintainer role line names the contest); the real-summary and judge-run fences ask a normal work request first.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
